title: Merge CLI + RPC paritytest harnesses behind shared caller abstraction
description:
## Summary

Simplifier + architect both flag this. paritytest has TWO harnesses (RPC-level DualRunner in runner.go, CLI-level in cli_parity_test.go) with near-identical: spawn code, fixture loader, variable substitution, differ.

## Fix

Extract a \`Caller\` interface:

\`\`\`go
type Caller interface {
    Call(ctx context.Context, method string, params json.RawMessage) (map[string]any, error)
}
\`\`\`

Two implementations: \`BackendCaller{backend.IssueBackend}\` (RPC-level) and \`ExecCaller{bd|fdb}\` (CLI). Single fixture bank, single differ, single report format.

## Scope

~300 lines deleted net. Medium risk — the CLI harness has a forked ignore list that needs reconciliation.

## When

After H1 (FleetBackend unification) lands, since that deletes fleetadapter.go and changes the callsite.

title: Waiver lifecycle: waiver_class (permanent vs pending_fix) — upstream fleet-db
description:
## Summary

Sprint churn (removed all 6 waivers → restored 001/002/003) demonstrated the contract schema lacks typing. No way to distinguish "permanent architectural decision" from "temporary cover-for-pending-bug-fix" waivers.

## Fix (upstream in fleet-db's contract.schema.json)

- Add \`waiver_class: permanent | pending_fix\`
- Require \`target_fix_ticket\` (ID reference) when class=pending_fix
- Require \`expires\` date on pending_fix
- On ticket close: auto-flip pending_fix waiver to failing (harness re-enforces)

## Pairs with

Harness update to consume the new field.

## When

Low priority — process improvement, not a blocker. File upstream; track separately.

title: Pin fleet-db binary provenance: single source for Go spawn + docker compose
description:
## Summary

Architect concern: paritytest Go subprocess spawning uses \`/tmp/fleet-db\` (built from \`~/codebase/fleet-db\` HEAD); docker-compose builds its own image from the same source context. No single pinning, so CI runs could use different binaries without signal.

## Fix

\`make parity-fleet-db-bin\` builds \`/tmp/fleet-db\` from a pinned SHA. Both harnesses depend on that target before running. Compose stack uses a buildarg referencing the same SHA.

## When

After UI + CLI harnesses are stable; low urgency.

title: Loom webui: auto-bootstrap workspace on LOOM_SEED_WORKSPACE env var (unblocks UI parity)
description:
## Summary

UI parity suite (test/parity/ui/) and docker-compose stack (test/parity/docker-compose.parity.yml) are fully implemented and the stack comes up cleanly (verified 2026-04-23). The only remaining blocker to running the 14 Playwright specs is that **loom-fleet has no webui workspace at startup** and can't be bootstrapped via the webui API because loom's workspace model requires a repos array.

## Reproduction

\`\`\`bash
podman-compose -f test/parity/docker-compose.parity.yml up -d
# All 5 services start; loom-fleet is healthy and responsive
curl http://localhost:8082/api/workspaces
# → {"success":true,"workspaces":[]}

curl -X POST http://localhost:8082/api/workspaces -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
    -d '{"name":"PARITY","path":"/workspace","type":"empty"}'
# → {"error":"repos is required for empty workspace type","kind":"validation_error"}
\`\`\`

## Fix

Add an env-driven auto-bootstrap to loom serve:

- \`LOOM_SEED_WORKSPACE=<name>\` (optional)
- On startup, if set AND no workspace with that name exists, create one with synthesized safe-defaults (path=/workspace, type=empty, repos=[{path:"/workspace",name:"default"}])
- Skip if any workspace exists already (idempotent)

Useful beyond parity testing: CI containers, ephemeral demo stacks, dev containers.

## Acceptance

- Setting LOOM_SEED_WORKSPACE=PARITY on loom-fleet's container results in GET /api/workspaces listing a workspace
- \`test/parity/seed.sh\` can POST to /api/workspaces/{id}/issues on loom-fleet without extra setup
- \`make test-parity-ui\` runs all 14 specs to completion

## Why here, not in seed.sh

seed.sh is a fixture-loading script; shouldn't be the thing that designs loom's workspace bootstrap. This belongs in loom itself.

## Companion

Full context in docs/design/parity-report-2026-04-22/webui-gaps.md §"Why loom-fleet bootstrap fails" + §"Two ways forward".

**Architect finding — constructor signatures incorrect in description:**

- Wrong: `beadsbackend.New(rpc.Client)`

title: P2.2 Write fixtures for loomcli-extended IssueBackend methods
description:
Author parity fixtures for the IssueBackend methods that fleet-db's existing harness does NOT cover (because they're loomcli-internal use cases).

## Methods to fixture
- SearchIssues(query, limit) — full-text relevance ranking
- GetMutations(sinceMs) — polling for SSE
- WaitForMutations(sinceMs, timeoutMs) — long-poll
- Batch(ops) — atomic multi-op (verify all-or-nothing)
- ListEvents(id, limit) — per-issue audit trail
- GetChildren(id) — epic children query
- DeferIssue(id, until) / UndeferIssue(id) — scheduling
- RemoveLabel(id, label) — label deletion (add is already covered)

## Format
JSONL fixtures matching fleet-db's test/fixtures/ layout. Each fixture: setup, ops, expected.

## Hypotheses to validate
- fleet-db may not implement GetMutations/WaitForMutations (loomcli SSE depends on these)
- SearchIssues ranking semantics may differ from beads SQLite FTS
- Batch atomicity may differ

comments.author: architect-review
comments.text:
**Architect finding — hypothesized fleet-db gaps don't exist; reframe Phase 2 around loomcli adapter gaps:**

All four "missing" methods exist in fleet-db's HTTP API (verified via `~/codebase/fleet-db/api/openapi.yaml`):
- `SearchIssues` → `GET /api/v1/{ws}/issues/search?q=` (openapi.yaml:428)
- `GetMutations` → `GET /api/v1/{ws}/events/mutations` (openapi.yaml:1292)
- `WaitForMutations` → same endpoint with `timeout` long-poll
- `GetChildren` → `GET /api/v1/{ws}/issues/{id}/children` (openapi.yaml:907)
- `RemoveLabel` → present in 19-op contract at `parity_test.go:344`

**The actual gaps are in loomcli's FleetBackend adapter** — these methods return `ErrNotImplemented` today:
- `Batch()` — `internal/backend/fleet/fleet.go:553`
- `GetMutations()` — `fleet.go:559`
- `WaitForMutations()` — `fleet.go:563`
- `Count()` — `fleet.go:266`
- `Stats()` — partial (missing `ReadyIssues`, `EpicsEligibleForClosure`, `AverageLeadTime`); see comment at fleet.go:238 referencing fleet-db ticket `fleet-08yg`

**Real Batch gap:** fleet-db has `POST /batch` (create-only) and `POST /batch/close` (close-only). Loomcli's `IssueBackend.Batch(ops []BatchOp)` accepts mixed operations — no single-endpoint fan-in exists. The adapter must fan-out across endpoints, and atomicity semantics differ from beads. This is the real gap to validate.

**Reframed Phase 2 hypothesis:** "Identify which IssueBackend methods need FleetBackend adapter implementation, and which require fleet-db server changes." Most gaps will be the former.

comments.author: implementation
comments.text: Closed with 4 fixtures landing (MVP + 3 new). Agent extended fleet adapter with Update/Close/Reopen, added auto-discovery test helper. Real signals surfaced: source_repo drift, close-result null projection bug in loomcli beads adapter, KindNotFound vs KindUnavailable error-classification drift in loomcli beads adapter. Follow-up fixtures proposed for deps, labels, comments, list-ordering, delete.

title: P2.3 Implement DualRunner: instantiate beads + fleet, execute fixtures
description:
Wire the parity package to spin up both backends and execute fixtures against each.

## Components
- beadsbackend.New(rpc.Client) wrapping a local bd daemon (or in-process beads.Server)
- fleet.New(Config{BaseURL, WorkspaceID}) pointing at a running fleet-db
- For each fixture: run the same op sequence against both, capture responses, normalize, diff

## Test setup helpers
- ensureBeadsDaemon(t) — start bd daemon in temp dir, return rpc.Client
- ensureFleetDB(t) — start (or reuse) fleet-db + redis via testcontainers
- normalizeResponse(...) — strip timestamps, sort lists, mask IDs (per fleet-db's normalizer.go)

comments.author: architect-review
comments.text:
**Architect finding — DualRunner viability + setup pattern:**

Both backends CAN coexist in a single test binary, but each requires a subprocess (no in-process embedding works):

**Beads side:**
- `BeadsBackend` wraps a `beadsClient` interface — production impl is `*rpc.Client` dialing a Unix socket to a running `bd` daemon
- Pattern: spawn `bd daemon start` in a `t.TempDir()` workspace, dial its socket, wrap with `beads.New()`
- `~/codebase/fleet-db/test/parity/parity_test.go` already has this pattern — mirror it

**Fleet side:**
- fleet-db's server packages are all `internal/` (only `pkg/client/` is exported); CANNOT embed in-process from loomcli
- Pattern: `go build -o /tmp/fleet-db ~/codebase/fleet-db/cmd/fleet-db`, spawn on a random port, dial via `fleet.New(fleet.Config{BaseURL: "http://localhost:<port>"})`
- testcontainers is NOT needed; subprocess + port-scan is sufficient

**Blocker:** `scripts/check-no-raw-exec.sh` enforces no `exec.Command` in tests. Add `internal/backend/paritytest/` to its exclusion list. Otherwise the parity package fails the precommit check.

**Setup placement:** Use `TestMain` to spawn both daemons once for the package, not per-test. Spinup cost is otherwise prohibitive.

comments.author: implementation
comments.text: Closed. DualRunner landed in commit 9216533d — spawns bd daemon + fleet-db subprocess with embedded miniredis, loads JSON fixtures, executes steps on both backends, emits DiffEntry rows. Current dispatcher handles issue.create and issue.show; extension to more methods (update/close/reopen/etc.) is a continuation agent.

title: P2.4 Emit diff report in fleet-db-compatible format

## Schema (from fleet-db)
- summary: fixtures_run, steps_executed, total_comparisons, diffs_found, unapproved_diffs, waived_diffs
- fixtures: [{fixture_id, title, diffs, verdict}]
- verdict: pass|fail

comments.text:
**Architect finding — copy report types, don't import:**

The `Report`, `ReportSummary`, `FixtureReport`, `DiffEntry`, `WaiverUsage` types live in `~/codebase/fleet-db/test/parity/report.go` under `//go:build parity`. That path is not under `pkg/` — fleet-db's test packages are not externally importable.

**Action:** Copy the struct definitions (~60 lines) into `internal/backend/paritytest/report.go`. The JSON wire format matches exactly so consolidated reporting tooling reads both repos' outputs identically. Do NOT add a fleet-db Go module dep.

**Confirmed schema** (from `~/codebase/fleet-db/artifacts/parity/diff-report.json`):
- top-level: `version`, `generated_at`, `contract_version`, `mode`, `beads_available`, `summary`, `verdict`, `fixtures[]`, `waivers_used`, `warnings`
- `summary`: `fixtures_run`, `steps_executed`, `total_comparisons`, `diffs_found`, `unapproved_diffs`, `waived_diffs`, `normalized_diffs`, `expired_waivers`

description:
New top-level target that:
1. Builds bd binary (go install ./third_party/beads/cmd/bd)

title: Add loom init command for guided setup
description:
Add a 'loom init' command that helps users set up loom agents with an interactive guided experience. Should:
- Check for prerequisites (beads CLI, git worktrees directory)
- Initialize beads if not already done (bd init)
- Help create worktrees for agents (prompt for names like falcon, nova, etc.)
- Explain the loom workflow (plan → review → task)
- Answer common setup questions
- Optionally create sample tasks to get started
design:
## Summary

Add a `loom init` command that provides a guided, interactive setup experience for new users. This command will check prerequisites, initialize beads if needed, create worktrees for agents, and explain the loom workflow. It helps users go from zero to a working loom setup with minimal friction.

## Technical Approach

The command follows a step-by-step wizard pattern using standard Go library I/O (`bufio.Scanner`, `fmt.Print`) for interactive prompts. Each step validates its preconditions before proceeding and provides clear feedback on what was done. The command is idempotent where possible - it skips steps that are already complete.

**Key Design Decisions:**
- Use standard library only (no external prompt library) to keep dependencies minimal
- Make each step skippable/automatic if already done
- Provide `--yes` flag for non-interactive mode with sensible defaults
- Use existing utility functions from `worktree.go`, `git.go`, and `exec.go`

## Files to Create

### internal/cli/init.go
New file containing the `loom init` command implementation.

**Contents:**
- `initCmd` - cobra command definition with flags
- `runInit()` - main entry point
- `checkPrerequisites()` - verify bd and git are available
- `initBeads()` - initialize beads if not present
- `createWorktreesDir()` - create worktrees directory
- `createWorktrees()` - interactive worktree creation
- `showSummary()` - display final setup summary and next steps
- Helper functions for prompts: `promptYesNo()`, `promptString()`, `promptSelection()`

**Flags:**
- `--yes, -y` - Non-interactive mode with defaults
- `--worktrees-dir` - Override worktrees directory (default: from env or "worktrees")
- `--names` - Comma-separated worktree names for non-interactive mode (default: "falcon,nova")

## Files to Modify

### internal/cli/root.go
Add the init command to the root command.

**Changes:**
- Import the init command (automatic via `init()` pattern)
- No direct changes needed if using the `init()` function pattern

## Dependencies

- Standard library: `bufio`, `fmt`, `os`, `path/filepath`, `strings`
- Internal: existing utilities from `worktree.go`, `git.go`, `exec.go`
- External: `bd` CLI must be installed (checked at runtime)

## Edge Cases and Error Handling

1. **bd CLI not installed**: Check with `which bd` or `bd --version`. Display clear installation instructions from the root.go help text.

2. **Not a git repository**: Check for `.git` directory or run `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`. Fail with helpful message.

3. **beads already initialized**: Check for `.beads/` directory. Skip init step with message "beads already initialized, skipping..."

4. **Worktrees directory exists but empty**: Proceed with worktree creation.

5. **Worktrees directory has existing worktrees**: List them and ask if user wants to add more, or skip step.

6. **Worktree name conflicts**: If user enters a name that already exists, prompt for different name.

7. **Git worktree add fails**: Common causes: branch already exists, dirty working tree. Show the git error and suggest fixes.

8. **User cancels mid-setup**: Graceful exit with message about what was completed and how to resume.

9. **Permission errors**: Creating directories might fail. Catch and display permission error with path.

10. **Running from inside a worktree**: Detect if cwd is a worktree (not main repo) and warn user to run from main repo.

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests (internal/cli/init_test.go)

1. **TestCheckPrerequisites** - Test prerequisite checking
   - `bd` command available → success
   - `bd` command not found → error with install instructions
   - Not a git repo → error with message

2. **TestInitBeads** - Test beads initialization logic
   - `.beads/` exists → skip with message
   - `.beads/` does not exist → run `bd init`
   - `bd init` fails → error propagation

3. **TestCreateWorktrees** - Test worktree creation
   - Valid names → creates worktrees
   - Duplicate name → prompts for new name
   - Git error → shows error message

4. **TestNonInteractiveMode** - Test `--yes` flag
   - Uses default names (falcon, nova)
   - Respects `--names` override
   - Skips all prompts

### Integration Tests

Create a temp directory, init a git repo, run `loom init --yes`, verify:
- `.beads/` directory exists
- `worktrees/falcon` and `worktrees/nova` exist and are valid git worktrees
- Each worktree has correct branch checked out

### Manual Verification

1. Fresh setup: Clone a repo, run `loom init`, verify guided experience works
2. Partial setup: Have `.beads/` already, run `loom init`, verify it skips beads init
3. With existing worktrees: Verify it offers to add more or skip
4. Cancel during setup: Ctrl+C at various points, verify clean state
5. Non-interactive: `loom init --yes --names="alpha,beta,gamma"` creates 3 worktrees

## Implementation Notes

### Suggested Agent Names
Use the same naming convention from the lead prompt - fast things:
- falcon, nova, spark, ember, flux, pulse, dash, swift, bolt, comet

### Interactive Prompts Pattern
```go
func promptYesNo(prompt string, defaultYes bool) bool {
    reader := bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin)
    hint := "[y/N]"
    if defaultYes {
        hint = "[Y/n]"
    }
    fmt.Printf("%s %s ", prompt, hint)
    input, _ := reader.ReadString(\n)
    input = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(input))
    if input == "" {
        return defaultYes
    }
    return input == "y" || input == "yes"
}
```

### Step-by-Step Flow
```
$ loom init

🔧 Loom Setup Wizard
====================

Step 1: Prerequisites
✓ bd (beads CLI) found
✓ git repository detected

Step 2: Initialize beads
→ Creating .beads/ directory...
✓ beads initialized

Step 3: Create worktrees
How many agent worktrees? [2]: 
Name for worktree 1 [falcon]: 
→ Creating worktree falcon on branch falcon...
✓ Created worktrees/falcon

Name for worktree 2 [nova]: 
→ Creating worktree nova on branch nova...
✓ Created worktrees/nova

Setup complete\! 🎉

Directory structure:
  .beads/           Issue database
  worktrees/
    falcon/         Agent workspace (branch: falcon)
    nova/           Agent workspace (branch: nova)

Next steps:
1. Create tasks:     bd create --title="My first task" --type=task
2. Run planner:      loom plan falcon
3. Review plans:     loom lead
4. Implement:        loom task falcon
5. Monitor:          loom monitor
```
close_reason: Implemented loom init command with interactive setup wizard, prerequisites check, beads initialization, worktree creation, and comprehensive tests

title: Make ConcurrencyTracker.Acquire check closed for unlimited roles
description: ConcurrencyTracker.Acquire for unlimited roles (concurrency.go:46-51) increments count and returns true without checking the closed flag. TryAcquire does check closed for unlimited roles. Make behavior consistent. Safe in practice due to outer shutdown checks but creates API inconsistency. From PR #11 review.
design:
## Summary

`ConcurrencyTracker.Acquire` for unlimited roles (lines 46-51) increments the count and returns `true` without checking the `closed` flag. `TryAcquire` correctly checks `closed` before acquiring for unlimited roles (line 73-75). This creates an API inconsistency where `Acquire` can succeed after shutdown for unlimited roles. The fix is a one-line addition to check `closed` in the unlimited-role early-return path.

## Technical Approach

Add a `closed` check in the unlimited-role branch of `Acquire`, matching the pattern already used in `TryAcquire`.

## Files to Modify

### 1. `internal/cli/concurrency.go`

Change lines 46-51 from:
```go
	limit := ct.limits[role]
	if limit == 0 {
		// Unlimited — always acquire immediately
		ct.counts[role]++
		return true
	}
```

To:
```go
	limit := ct.limits[role]
	if limit == 0 {
		if ct.closed {
			return false
		}
		ct.counts[role]++
		return true
	}
```

This matches the pattern in `TryAcquire` (lines 73-75) where `closed` is checked before any acquisition.

### 2. `internal/cli/concurrency_test.go`

Add a test `TestConcurrencyTracker_AcquireUnlimitedAfterClose`:
```go
func TestConcurrencyTracker_AcquireUnlimitedAfterClose(t *testing.T) {
	ct := NewConcurrencyTracker(map[string]RoleConfig{
		"unlimited": {}, // no MaxConcurrency = unlimited
	})
	ct.Close()
	if ct.Acquire("unlimited") {
		t.Error("Acquire on closed tracker should return false for unlimited roles")
	}
}
```

## Files to Create

None.

## Dependencies

None.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Race condition**: The `closed` check is under the mutex, so no race exists.
2. **Nil receiver**: The nil check on line 40-42 returns before reaching this code, so no impact.
3. **Already-acquired unlimited roles**: Existing acquires are unaffected. Only new acquires after `Close()` will return false.

## Testing Strategy

1. Run the new test `TestConcurrencyTracker_AcquireUnlimitedAfterClose` — should pass.
2. Run all existing concurrency tests: `go test ./internal/cli/... -run TestConcurrency` — should pass.
3. Run the existing `TestDaemonStop_ClosesConcurrencyTracker` — should still pass (it tests limited roles).
close_reason: Completed: added closed check in Acquire for unlimited roles, matching TryAcquire pattern. New test added.

title: Add PTY integration tests for TTY detection (Layer 2)
description:
Add PTY-based integration tests that prove TTY detection works end-to-end using github.com/creack/pty (already in go.mod).

Approach:
- Go test subprocess pattern (os.Args[0] + -test.run=TestHelper) as mock backends
- Mock helpers check isatty(stdin) via unix.IoctlGetTermios
- Exit codes: 0=TTY detected, 1=no TTY, 2=invalid args
- pty.Start() allocates real PTY for subprocess
- Gated behind LOOM_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 env var

Tests:
- TestClaudeInteractiveWithPTY - verify TTY detected
- TestClaudeInteractiveWithoutPTY - verify error without TTY
- TestCodexInteractiveWithPTY
- TestOpenCodeInteractiveWithPTY

Files to create:
- internal/cli/backend_pty_integration_test.go
design:
## Summary

This task adds PTY-based integration tests that prove TTY detection works end-to-end for the backend interactive invokers. When a backend (claude, codex, opencode) launches in interactive mode, it sets cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin — if the process is running with a real TTY, the subprocess should detect that its stdin is a TTY. These tests use github.com/creack/pty (already in go.mod) to allocate a real PTY for a mock subprocess, and the Go test subprocess pattern (os.Args[0] + -test.run=TestHelperXxx) to create a mock backend binary that checks isatty(stdin) via golang.org/x/sys/unix.IoctlGetTermios. Tests are gated behind LOOM_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 since they allocate real PTYs and run subprocesses.

This task depends on loomcli-jux which extracts buildXxxInteractiveCmd() functions from the invokers. These builder functions are necessary because the tests need to construct the cmd without executing it via cmd.Run(), then use pty.Start(cmd) to run it with a real PTY attached.

## Technical Approach

**Pattern: Go test subprocess + PTY.** The standard Go testing pattern for testing subprocess behavior is to re-exec the test binary itself with -test.run=TestHelperXxx. The TestHelper function detects it's being run as a subprocess (via env var like GO_WANT_HELPER_PROCESS=1), performs the real work (checks isatty), and exits. The parent test uses pty.Start() to launch the subprocess with a real PTY, then checks the exit code to verify TTY detection.

**Why not just check cmd.Stdin == os.Stdin?** Layer 1 (loomcli-jux) already tests that cmd.Stdin == os.Stdin at the pointer level. This Layer 2 goes further: it proves that when a PTY is attached, the subprocess actually sees a TTY on its stdin. This catches issues that pointer equality alone cannot: misconfigured file descriptors, PTY allocation failures, or platform-specific TTY behavior.

**Exit code protocol for mock helpers:**
- 0 = TTY detected on stdin (isatty returns true)
- 1 = No TTY detected (isatty returns false)
- 2 = Invalid arguments / error

**Gating:** All tests check for LOOM_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 at the top and call t.Skip() if not set. This prevents PTY-allocating tests from running in CI environments where PTYs may not be available.

## Files to Create

### 1. internal/cli/backend_pty_integration_test.go

Single file containing all PTY integration tests and test helper subprocess functions.

**Test helpers (mock backend subprocesses):**

```go
// TestHelperProcess is the subprocess entry point for PTY integration tests.
// When invoked as a subprocess (GO_WANT_HELPER_PROCESS=1), it checks whether
// stdin is a TTY using unix.IoctlGetTermios and exits with code 0 (TTY) or 1 (no TTY).
func TestHelperProcess(t *testing.T) {
    if os.Getenv("GO_WANT_HELPER_PROCESS") != "1" {
        return
    }
    // Check isatty on stdin (fd 0)
    _, err := unix.IoctlGetTermios(int(os.Stdin.Fd()), unix.TIOCGETA) // TIOCGETA on darwin, TCGETS on linux
    if err != nil {
        os.Exit(1) // Not a TTY
    }
    os.Exit(0) // Is a TTY
}
```

Note: Use the ioctlReadTermios platform constant. On macOS it's unix.TIOCGETA, on Linux it's unix.TCGETS. The simplest approach is to use a build-tag-guarded helper or use the `term` package, but since we already have golang.org/x/sys/unix, we can use a platform-aware constant. Since this project targets darwin (per the environment), use unix.TIOCGETA with a //go:build darwin tag, or better yet, use unix.IoctlGetTermios with the TIOCGETA/TCGETS constant selected via a small platform file. However, the simplest portable approach is:

```go
func isTerminal(fd int) bool {
    _, err := unix.IoctlGetTermios(fd, ioctlReadTermios)
    return err == nil
}
```

With `ioctlReadTermios` defined in platform-specific files (or just use a build tag on the test file itself since tests only need to run on the dev platform).

**Actually, the simplest approach:** Since golang.org/x/sys/unix already provides the platform-abstracted `unix.IoctlGetTermios`, and the ioctl constant differs by OS, we should define it with build tags. But since this is a test file and the project runs on macOS:
- Use `//go:build darwin` for now and `unix.TIOCGETA`
- Or use the portable approach: create a tiny helper that tries both constants

**Recommended approach:** Use `golang.org/x/term` package's `term.IsTerminal()` which handles cross-platform. But that adds a new dependency. Instead, use `unix.IoctlGetTermios` with a platform constant defined via a simple conditional:

```go
//go:build unix

import "golang.org/x/sys/unix"

func isTerminal(fd int) bool {
    // Try platform-specific ioctl
    _, err := unix.IoctlGetTermios(fd, unix.TIOCGETA)
    return err == nil
}
```

On Linux, TIOCGETA doesn't exist but TCGETS does. Since the go.mod targets macOS (darwin), we can use `//go:build darwin` and `unix.TIOCGETA`. For broader compatibility, add a `//go:build linux` variant with `unix.TCGETS` in a separate file. But for this task's scope (integration tests that run on the developer's machine), a single `//go:build darwin` file is sufficient, with a note to add Linux support if needed.

**REVISED SIMPLEST APPROACH:** Actually, `unix.IoctlGetTermios` on Linux accepts `unix.TCGETS` automatically. The constant name varies by platform:
- Darwin: `unix.TIOCGETA` 
- Linux: `unix.TCGETS`

But Go's `golang.org/x/sys/unix` package defines both on each platform. Let's verify this at implementation time. If not, create two small files. For the design, assume we need platform constants.

**Test functions:**

1. **TestClaudeInteractiveWithPTY** — Verifies that when a Claude interactive command is run with a real PTY, the subprocess detects stdin as a TTY.
   - Calls `buildClaudeInteractiveCmd()` (from loomcli-jux) to get the *exec.Cmd
   - Overrides cmd.Path and cmd.Args to point at the test binary (os.Args[0]) with -test.run=TestHelperProcess
   - Sets GO_WANT_HELPER_PROCESS=1 in cmd.Env
   - Uses `pty.Start(cmd)` to launch with a real PTY
   - Reads output, waits for exit
   - Asserts exit code 0 (TTY detected)

2. **TestClaudeInteractiveWithoutPTY** — Verifies that WITHOUT a PTY (using a pipe instead), the subprocess does NOT detect a TTY.
   - Same as above but uses cmd.Start() instead of pty.Start()
   - Pipes stdin from an os.Pipe (no TTY)
   - Asserts exit code 1 (no TTY detected)

3. **TestCodexInteractiveWithPTY** — Same as TestClaudeInteractiveWithPTY but uses `buildCodexInteractiveCmd()`.

4. **TestOpenCodeInteractiveWithPTY** — Same but uses `buildOpenCodeInteractiveCmd()`.

**Important design decision:** The buildXxxInteractiveCmd() functions (from loomcli-jux) construct commands that point to the real binary ("claude", "codex", "opencode"). For PTY tests, we need to override cmd.Path and cmd.Args to point at our test helper subprocess. The test will:
1. Call the builder to get a *exec.Cmd (this verifies the builder works)
2. Replace cmd.Path with os.Args[0] (the test binary)
3. Replace cmd.Args with [os.Args[0], "-test.run=TestHelperProcess", "--"]
4. Add GO_WANT_HELPER_PROCESS=1 to cmd.Env (preserving existing env vars from the builder)
5. Use pty.Start(cmd) to run with PTY

This ensures the test validates both the builder's configuration AND actual PTY TTY detection. The key insight is that cmd.Stdin must remain as os.Stdin (pointer equality, set by the builder), and pty.Start() will override it with the PTY's slave fd — which IS a TTY. If the builder had set stdin to a pipe, pty.Start() would still override it, so the test specifically validates that pty.Start() + the builder's cmd configuration results in TTY detection.

**Alternative simpler approach:** Since pty.Start() always overrides stdin/stdout/stderr with the PTY slave, the builder's cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin setting doesn't directly matter for the PTY test. What matters is: (1) the build step succeeds, and (2) when pty.Start() is used, the subprocess sees a TTY. The "without PTY" test is the complement: it proves that without pty.Start(), just using cmd.Start() with a pipe stdin, the subprocess does NOT see a TTY.

**Test structure pattern:**

```go
func skipUnlessIntegration(t *testing.T) {
    t.Helper()
    if os.Getenv("LOOM_INTEGRATION_TESTS") != "1" {
        t.Skip("skipping integration test (set LOOM_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 to run)")
    }
}

func TestClaudeInteractiveWithPTY(t *testing.T) {
    skipUnlessIntegration(t)
    
    cmd := exec.Command(os.Args[0], "-test.run=TestHelperProcess", "--")
    cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "GO_WANT_HELPER_PROCESS=1")
    
    ptmx, err := pty.Start(cmd)
    if err != nil {
        t.Fatalf("pty.Start failed: %v", err)
    }
    defer ptmx.Close()
    
    // Read any output (drain PTY to prevent blocking)
    go io.Copy(io.Discard, ptmx)
    
    err = cmd.Wait()
    if err != nil {
        t.Errorf("expected exit code 0 (TTY detected), got error: %v", err)
    }
}
```

### 2. internal/cli/isatty_darwin_test.go (if needed)

If `unix.TIOCGETA` is darwin-only and we need a separate Linux constant file:

```go
//go:build darwin

package cli

import "golang.org/x/sys/unix"

const ioctlReadTermios = unix.TIOCGETA
```

### 3. internal/cli/isatty_linux_test.go (if needed)

```go
//go:build linux

package cli

import "golang.org/x/sys/unix"

const ioctlReadTermios = unix.TCGETS
```

These small files keep the main test file clean and platform-agnostic. If the implementation discovers that unix.TIOCGETA is defined on Linux too (it isn't — it's darwin-only), then a single file suffices.

## Files to Modify

None. This task only creates new test files.

## Dependencies

- **github.com/creack/pty v1.1.24** — Already in go.mod. Used for pty.Start().
- **golang.org/x/sys v0.40.0** — Already in go.mod. Used for unix.IoctlGetTermios and TIOCGETA/TCGETS constants.
- **loomcli-jux (Layer 1)** — Must be completed first. Provides buildClaudeInteractiveCmd(), buildCodexInteractiveCmd(), buildOpenCodeInteractiveCmd() functions. The PTY tests verify end-to-end behavior that builds on the command construction these functions provide.

Note: The tests don't strictly NEED the buildXxxInteractiveCmd() functions — they could construct the test command independently. However, using the builders validates the integration between Layer 1 and Layer 2. If loomcli-jux is delayed, the implementation can proceed by constructing commands directly, but the design assumes loomcli-jux is complete.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

- **PTY allocation failure:** On some CI environments, PTY allocation may fail. The `skipUnlessIntegration()` guard prevents these tests from running unless explicitly enabled. Tests should use t.Fatalf on pty.Start() failure with a clear message.
- **Subprocess deadlock:** The test subprocess (TestHelperProcess) must not use t.Log or any testing.T methods since it's running as a subprocess. It must communicate only via exit code. The parent must drain the PTY output (io.Copy to io.Discard) to prevent the subprocess from blocking on write.
- **Platform constants:** unix.TIOCGETA exists on darwin, unix.TCGETS on linux. Use build-tag-guarded files to select the correct constant. The TestHelperProcess needs this to call IoctlGetTermios.
- **Race condition with PTY close:** After pty.Start(), the parent must wait for cmd.Wait() before closing the PTY master fd. If the master is closed too early, the slave gets SIGHUP and the test sees an unexpected signal death.
- **TestHelperProcess detection:** The GO_WANT_HELPER_PROCESS=1 env var distinguishes real test execution from subprocess execution. Without this check, TestHelperProcess would exit(0) during normal test runs, which would confuse the test runner.
- **Lingering subprocess:** If the test times out, the subprocess could linger. Use t.Cleanup() to kill the process and close the PTY.

## Testing Strategy

**Integration tests gated behind LOOM_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1.**

Run with:
```bash
LOOM_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestClaudeInteractiveWith -v
LOOM_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestCodexInteractiveWith -v
LOOM_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestOpenCodeInteractiveWith -v
```

Run all PTY tests:
```bash
LOOM_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 go test ./internal/cli/ -run "Interactive.*PTY" -v
```

Verify skip behavior (should show SKIP, not FAIL):
```bash
go test ./internal/cli/ -run "Interactive.*PTY" -v
```

Full package test (PTY tests skipped):
```bash
go test ./internal/cli/ -v -count=1
```

Manual verification:
1. Run with LOOM_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 — all 4 tests pass
2. Run without the env var — all 4 tests show "SKIP"
3. Verify TestHelperProcess doesn't produce output during normal test runs (the env var guard returns immediately)
4. Verify no PTY file descriptor leaks (lsof during/after test should show no stale PTY fds)

title: API spec: Terminal session lifecycle

design:
# API Spec: Terminal Session Lifecycle

## Summary

This task documents the complete REST + WebSocket API for terminal session lifecycle management, using workspace-scoped routes per the n28bt epic direction. These endpoints govern creating, connecting to, monitoring, restarting, killing, and seeding terminal sessions backed by tmux. The spec covers authentication (one-time HMAC tokens), the WebSocket binary relay protocol (including the corrected in-band resize format), session limits, crash detection close codes, and deferred kill scheduling. All routes use the `/api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/...` path prefix with WorkspaceMiddleware validation. It excludes tab metadata CRUD (loomcli-wit5o), state persistence (loomcli-uzq7i), session history (loomcli-rocpq), and issue-linked session queries (loomcli-aeilf).

## Revision Changes

This revision addresses feedback from the 2026-03-28 review:

1. **Route count reconciliation** — The flat terminal mux block (routes.go lines 108-133) contains 15 route registrations total: 13 in the outer `termManager != nil` block (12 unconditional + 1 gated on termAuth) and 2 in the nested `tabMetaStore != nil` block. This spec covers 10 of the 13 session-relevant routes. The remaining 5 routes belong to loomcli-uzq7i (terminal state persistence) and are now explicitly listed in the "Out of Scope" section with exact paths and line numbers.
2. **Workspace-scoped paths** (carried forward from 2026-03-27 revision) — All endpoints use `/api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/...` per n28bt epic direction.
3. **Resize protocol correction** (carried forward) — Documents the correct 5-byte format `[0x01, cols_hi, cols_lo, rows_hi, rows_lo]`.
4. **IssueID correction** (carried forward) — GET sessions response does NOT include `issue_id` field.

## Scope — Endpoints Covered

The flat terminal mux block in routes.go (lines 108-133) contains 15 route registrations total. This spec covers **10 session lifecycle endpoints** (mapped to workspace-scoped paths) plus **3 agent-terminal variants** (already workspace-scoped on wsMux). The remaining 5 routes in the flat block belong to loomcli-uzq7i and are explicitly excluded below in "Out of Scope".

**Session lifecycle endpoints (this spec — 10 routes from flat mux):**

1. `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/token` — one-time token generation (routes.go:111, gated on termAuth)
2. `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/ws` — WebSocket terminal relay (routes.go:113)
3. `POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/spawn` — pre-create tmux session (routes.go:117)
4. `POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/restart` — kill + recreate session with current backend (routes.go:114)
5. `POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/kill` — forcibly kill session (routes.go:115)
6. `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/session-status` — check session liveness (routes.go:116)
7. `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/sessions` — list active sessions (routes.go:109)
8. `POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/sessions/{name}/seed` — inject issue context via tmux send-keys (routes.go:118)
9. `POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/sessions/{session}/kill` — schedule deferred kill (30s grace) (routes.go:122)
10. `POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/sessions/close-all` — kill all sessions + cleanup metadata (routes.go:123)

**Agent-terminal variants (already workspace-scoped on wsMux, routes.go:261-267):**
- `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/agents/{name}/terminal/token`
- `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/agents/{name}/terminal/ws`
- `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/agents/{name}/terminal/info`

## Technical Approach

### Format
Replace the existing sparse Terminal section in docs/api.md (lines 743-770) with a full "Terminal Session Lifecycle" section. Follow established doc conventions: auth line, parameter tables, JSON response bodies, error cases per-endpoint.

### Workspace-Scoped Routing
All session lifecycle endpoints use the `/api/workspaces/{ws}/` prefix, consistent with the pattern established by tab metadata routes (routes.go:236-244) and workspace-scoped issue routes (routes.go:200-208). The `{ws}` path parameter is the workspace identifier (UUID per n28bt epic). WorkspaceMiddleware (workspace_context.go:29-45) validates the workspace exists via `wsExists(id)` and injects the ID into the request context via `WithWorkspace()`.

**Current codebase state:** The flat terminal mux block (routes.go:108-133) contains 15 route registrations: 10 session lifecycle routes covered by this spec, 3 scrollback/export/scrollback-info routes belonging to loomcli-uzq7i (lines 119-121), and 2 terminal UI state routes also belonging to loomcli-uzq7i (lines 131-132). Agent terminal routes (lines 261-267) and tab metadata routes (lines 236-244) are already workspace-scoped on wsMux. The frontend terminal.ts has explicit `TODO(workspace-routing): migrate to wsUrl when workspace-scoped route lands` comments on all flat endpoints. This spec defines the target API surface that aligns the 10 session lifecycle routes under the workspace-scoped pattern.

**Implementation note:** Route migration from flat mux to wsMux is an implementation concern. The spec defines the target API. Handlers may need to call `WorkspaceFromContext(ctx)` to scope tmux session lookups.

### Validation Rules (cross-cutting)
- **Workspace ID** (`{ws}`): validated by WorkspaceMiddleware — returns 400 if empty, 404 if workspace not found
- **Session names**: regex `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$` — enforced on all endpoints that accept session names
- Dots in session names (from issue IDs) are sanitized to dashes before validation
- Request body limit: 1 MB (standard maxRequestBody)

### Authentication Model
- **Standard endpoints**: Bearer token via Authorization header, plus WorkspaceMiddleware validation
- **Token endpoint** (`GET .../terminal/token`): requires standard bearer auth, returns a one-time terminal token
- **WebSocket endpoint** (`GET .../terminal/ws`): uses one-time token via `?token=` query param. WorkspaceMiddleware validates the workspace. Standard bearer auth is not required for the WebSocket upgrade — the one-time token carries session identity and authorization.
- **Restart/Kill/Session-status**: require both bearer auth AND one-time terminal token via `?token=` query param

### CORRECTION: Resize Protocol
**The existing api.md line 767 is WRONG.** It documents a 4-byte uint32 (rows<<16|cols) format. The actual implementation (handlers_terminal.go:17-18, handlers_terminal_ws.go:263-265) uses a **5-byte format**:
- Byte 0: `0x01` (resizeMsgMarker, handlers_terminal.go:17)
- Bytes 1-2: cols as uint16 big-endian (binary.BigEndian.Uint16)
- Bytes 3-4: rows as uint16 big-endian (binary.BigEndian.Uint16)
- Total: resizeMsgLen = 5 (handlers_terminal.go:18)

### CORRECTION: IssueID in ListActiveSessions
The `terminalSessionInfo` struct declares `IssueID string json:"issue_id,omitempty"` but the `ListActiveSessions` handler only sets Name, Label, and Created. Because of `omitempty`, the field is always absent from the JSON response. Issue-to-session mapping is served by `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/sessions/by-issue` (documented in loomcli-wit5o). The spec must NOT document `issue_id` as a response field for endpoint #7.

## Conventions Established
- **Workspace-scoped terminal paths**: `/api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/...` prefix for all session lifecycle endpoints, consistent with sibling routes for tabs and agent terminals
- **`{ws}` parameter name**: matches all other workspace-scoped routes in routes.go (issues, agents, fleet, SSE, config)
- **Token auth for WebSocket**: one-time token via query param (not bearer auth) for the WS upgrade endpoint
- **Bearer+token dual auth**: restart, kill, and session-status require both bearer auth and one-time terminal token

## Files to Modify

### docs/api.md
**Replace lines 743-770 entirely** (the sparse/incorrect existing Terminal section) with the full workspace-scoped specification.

Structure within docs/api.md:
```
## Terminal Session Lifecycle

### Workspace Scoping
### Authentication: One-Time Tokens
### GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/token
### GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/ws (WebSocket)
  - Connection lifecycle
  - Binary relay protocol (5-byte resize format)
  - Close codes
  - Session limit behavior
### POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/spawn
### POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/restart
### POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/kill
### GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/session-status
### GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/sessions
### POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/sessions/{name}/seed
### POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/sessions/{session}/kill (Deferred)
### POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/sessions/close-all
### Agent Terminal Endpoints
  - GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/agents/{name}/terminal/token
  - GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/agents/{name}/terminal/ws
  - GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/agents/{name}/terminal/info
```

## Out of Scope (Needs Separate Task)

### Flat routes explicitly excluded from this spec (belong to loomcli-uzq7i)

The flat terminal mux block (routes.go:108-133) contains 5 route registrations that are NOT covered by this spec. They belong to **loomcli-uzq7i** (API spec: Terminal state persistence):

| Line | Flat Route | Handler | Reason for Exclusion |
|------|-----------|---------|---------------------|
| 119 | `GET /api/terminal/sessions/{session}/scrollback` | `handleGetScrollback` | Scrollback capture — state persistence scope |
| 120 | `GET /api/terminal/sessions/{session}/export` | `handleExportSession` | Session export — state persistence scope |
| 121 | `GET /api/terminal/sessions/{session}/scrollback-info` | `handleScrollbackInfo` | Buffer statistics — state persistence scope |
| 131 | `GET /api/terminal/state` | `handleGetTerminalState` | UI state (active tab) — state persistence scope |
| 132 | `PATCH /api/terminal/state` | `handlePatchTerminalState` | UI state mutation — state persistence scope |

These 5 routes are documented in loomcli-uzq7i's design under workspace-scoped paths: `GET/PATCH /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/state` and `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/sessions/{session}/scrollback|export|scrollback-info`.

### Other exclusions

- **Backend route migration** — Moving the 10 flat session lifecycle routes (routes.go:109-123, excluding lines 119-121) from main mux to wsMux with WorkspaceMiddleware. This is implementation work, not spec work. May need a dedicated task in the n28bt epic or as part of n28bt.41 (legacy flat routes cleanup).
- **Frontend migration** — Resolving `TODO(workspace-routing)` comments in terminal.ts to use `wsUrl()`. Already tracked by the TODO comments; will happen when backend routes land.
- **Tab metadata endpoints** — documented in loomcli-wit5o (already workspace-scoped on wsMux at routes.go:236-244)
- **Session history endpoints** — documented in loomcli-rocpq
- **Issue tab endpoints** — documented in loomcli-aeilf

## Endpoint Specifications (Content to Write)

### 1. GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/token
- Auth: Required (standard bearer token)
- Path params: `{ws}` — workspace ID (required, validated by WorkspaceMiddleware)
- Query: `session` (required, validated against session name regex)
- Response 200: `{"token": "<one-time-use-token>"}`
- Response 400: `{"error": "invalid session"}` — missing or invalid session name
- Response 404: `{"error": "workspace not found: {ws}"}` — WorkspaceMiddleware rejection
- Response 500: `{"error": "failed to generate token"}` — HMAC generation failure
- Cache-Control: `no-store` header set on response
- Token format: `base64url(JSON{session, exp, nonce}).base64url(HMAC-SHA256-signature)`
- Token lifetime: 60 seconds, single-use (nonce tracked server-side in memory)

### 2. GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/ws (WebSocket)
- Auth: One-time token via `?token=` query param (not bearer auth — token carries session identity and authorization)
- Path params: `{ws}` — workspace ID (required, validated by WorkspaceMiddleware)
- Query params:
  | Param   | Type   | Required | Description |
  |---------|--------|----------|-------------|
  | session | string | yes      | tmux session name |
  | token   | string | yes*     | one-time terminal token (*when auth enabled) |
- Pre-upgrade validation (returns HTTP JSON error before WebSocket upgrade):
  - 400: missing session, invalid session name
  - 401: terminal authentication failed (invalid/expired/replayed token)
  - 404: workspace not found
  - 503: terminal manager not initialized, or maximum terminal sessions reached (default 20, from `defaultMaxTerminalSessions` in terminal.go:73)
- WebSocket binary protocol:
  - All frames are binary (websocket.MessageBinary)
  - Server->Client: raw PTY output bytes (read buffer 4096 bytes, `terminalReadBufSize`)
  - Client->Server: raw terminal input bytes OR resize message
  - **Resize message format (in-band): exactly 5 bytes**
    - Byte 0: `0x01` (resizeMsgMarker)
    - Bytes 1-2: cols as uint16 big-endian
    - Bytes 3-4: rows as uint16 big-endian
    - Example: 80x24 = `[0x01, 0x00, 0x50, 0x00, 0x18]`
    - **NOTE: Replaces the incorrect existing docs (line 767) that described a 4-byte uint32 (rows<<16|cols) format**
  - Max terminal size: 500 cols x 200 rows (`maxTerminalCols`, `maxTerminalRows` in handlers_terminal.go:19-20). Values exceeding these are silently ignored (no error returned).
  - Zero values for cols or rows: silently ignored (no resize performed)
  - Read limit: 32KB per WebSocket message (`wsReadLimit = 32768`, handlers_terminal.go:21)
  - Default terminal size: 80x24 (frontend sends resize immediately after connect)
  - Non-matching binary messages (wrong length or missing 0x01 marker): treated as regular terminal input, written to PTY
- Close codes:
  | Code | Constant | Meaning | Frontend behavior |
  |------|----------|---------|-------------------|
  | 1000 | StatusNormalClosure | Normal closure / session detached | Allow reconnect |
  | 4001 | wsCloseBackendExited (handlers_terminal_ws.go:161) | Backend process exited (crash) | Show CrashOverlay, NO auto-reconnect |
- Close reason (on 4001): last 10 lines of PTY output, truncated to 123 bytes (UTF-8-safe) for WebSocket close frame
- Session creation: if tmux session does not exist, `Attach()` creates it with the default command. Session is workspace-scoped (prefixed by workspace ID per n28bt.7).
- Deferred kill cancellation: if a pending scheduled kill exists for this session, `CancelPendingKill()` is called on attach
- SSE broadcast: if session is linked to an issue (via tab metadata), broadcasts `terminal_session_change` event on connect

### 3. POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/spawn
- Auth: Required (standard bearer token)
- Path params: `{ws}` — workspace ID (required)
- Request body:
  ```json
  {
    "session_name": "string (required)",
    "backend": "string (required — claude|codex|shell|gemini|etc.)"
  }
  ```
- Session name sanitization: dots replaced with dashes before validation
- Valid backends: claude, codex, gemini, shell (and others per `isValidBackend()`)
- Shell backend: uses default shell command instead of loom lead
- Response 200:
  ```json
  {
    "success": true,
    "data": {
      "session_name": "sanitized-name",
      "backend": "claude",
      "command": "claude",
      "created": true
    }
  }
  ```
  - `created`: false if tmux session already existed (idempotent)
- Response 400: missing session_name, missing backend, invalid session name, invalid backend
- Response 404: workspace not found
- Response 413: request body too large (>1 MB)
- Response 500: tmux spawn failure
- Response 503: terminal manager not initialized
- Side effect: for issue-linked sessions (matching pattern `issue-{project}-{number}`), records session in session history store with workspace ID
- Default terminal size for spawn: 120x40

### 4. POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/restart
- Auth: Required (standard bearer + one-time terminal token)
- Path params: `{ws}` — workspace ID (required)
- Query params: `session` (required), `token` (required when auth enabled)
- Behavior: kills existing tmux session, reads current backend from loom.yaml via daemon, updates default command, returns new backend name
- Shell tab special case: sessions starting with "lead-shell-" are killed without changing defaultCommand; returns `{"success": true, "backend": "shell"}`
- Response 200: `{"success": true, "backend": "claude"}`
- Response 400: missing session, invalid session name, invalid backend in loom.yaml
- Response 401: terminal authentication failed
- Response 404: workspace not found
- Response 405: method not allowed (non-POST)
- Response 503: terminal manager not initialized
- Note: does NOT create the new session — the frontend reconnects via WebSocket which triggers Attach()

### 5. POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/kill
- Auth: Required (standard bearer + one-time terminal token)
- Path params: `{ws}` — workspace ID (required)
- Query params: `session` (required), `token` (required when auth enabled)
- Response 200: `{"success": true}`
- Response 400: `{"success": false, "error": "invalid session"}`
- Response 401: terminal authentication failed
- Response 404: workspace not found
- Response 405: method not allowed (non-POST)
- Response 503: terminal manager not initialized
- Note: immediate kill, no grace period (contrast with deferred kill in endpoint #9)

### 6. GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/session-status
- Auth: Required (standard bearer + one-time terminal token)
- Path params: `{ws}` — workspace ID (required)
- Query params: `session` (required), `token` (required when auth enabled)
- Response 200 (alive): `{"alive": true}`
- Response 200 (dead — session gone or pane dead):
  ```json
  {
    "alive": false,
    "exit_reason": "last 10 lines of terminal output"
  }
  ```
  - `exit_reason`: only present if capture succeeds
  - Checks both tmux session existence AND pane liveness (process may have exited but tmux session lingers)
- Response 400: invalid session
- Response 401: terminal authentication failed
- Response 404: workspace not found
- Response 503: terminal manager not initialized

### 7. GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/sessions
- Auth: Required (standard bearer token)
- Path params: `{ws}` — workspace ID (required)
- No query params
- Response 200:
  ```json
  {
    "success": true,
    "data": {
      "sessions": [
        {
          "name": "talk-to-lead",
          "label": "talk-to-lead",
          "created": 1711108800
        }
      ]
    }
  }
  ```
  - **NOTE: The `terminalSessionInfo` struct declares `issue_id` with `json:"issue_id,omitempty"` but the handler NEVER populates it — it is always omitted from the JSON response. Issue-to-session mapping is served by `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/sessions/by-issue` (documented in loomcli-wit5o). Do NOT document `issue_id` as a response field.**
  - "talk-to-lead" is always included (`created`=0 if not yet spawned)
  - Sessions are filtered by server's `sessionPrefix` (workspace-scoped isolation per n28bt.7)
  - `created`: Unix timestamp, 0 if session not yet created in tmux
- Response 404: workspace not found
- Response 500: tmux list-sessions failure
- Response 503: terminal manager not initialized

### 8. POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/sessions/{name}/seed
- Auth: Required (standard bearer token)
- Path params: `{ws}` — workspace ID (required), `{name}` — session name
- Request body:
  ```json
  {
    "issue_id": "string (required)",
    "title": "string (required)",
    "description": "string (optional, truncated to 800 chars)",
    "design": "string (optional, truncated to 500 chars)",
    "blockers": [
      {"id": "string", "title": "string"}
    ]
  }
  ```
  - `blockers`: max 5 included in prompt
- Behavior: formats a context prompt and injects it into the running tmux session via tmux send-keys
- Response 200: `{"success": true}`
- Response 400: missing session name, invalid JSON, missing issue_id or title
- Response 404: workspace not found; or `{"success": false, "error": "session not found: {name}"}` — tmux session does not exist
- Response 500: tmux send-keys failure
- Response 503: terminal manager not initialized

### 9. POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/sessions/{session}/kill (Deferred)
- Auth: Required (standard bearer token)
- Path params: `{ws}` — workspace ID (required), `{session}` — session name (validated via `tabmeta.ValidateSessionName`)
- No request body
- Behavior: schedules a kill after 30-second grace period. Cancelled if user re-attaches via WebSocket before timeout fires (CancelPendingKill in Attach).
- Response 200: `{"success": true}`
- Response 400: invalid session name
- Response 404: workspace not found
- Response 503: terminal manager not initialized

### 10. POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/sessions/close-all
- Auth: Required (standard bearer token)
- Path params: `{ws}` — workspace ID (required)
- No request body
- Behavior:
  1. Kill all tmux sessions (by workspace-scoped prefix per n28bt.7)
  2. Delete all tab metadata for this workspace (Redis cleanup)
  3. Broadcast SSE `terminal_session_change` event
- Response 200 (clean): `{"success": true}`
- Response 200 (partial): `{"success": true, "warning": "sessions killed but metadata cleanup incomplete"}`
- Response 404: workspace not found
- Response 500: tmux kill failure
- Response 503: terminal manager not initialized

### Agent Terminal Endpoints

These mirror the main terminal endpoints but are scoped to individual agent sessions. They are **already registered as workspace-scoped routes** in routes.go:261-267 on wsMux behind WorkspaceMiddleware.

#### GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/agents/{name}/terminal/token
- Auth: Required (standard bearer token)
- Path params: `{ws}` — workspace ID, `{name}` — agent name
- Session name: derived from agent name (prefixed with workspace-scoped session prefix)
- Response/errors: same shape as main token endpoint (#1)

#### GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/agents/{name}/terminal/ws
- Auth: One-time token via `?token=` query param
- Path params: `{ws}` — workspace ID, `{name}` — agent name
- Query params: `token` (required when auth enabled)
- Session name: derived from agent name
- WebSocket protocol: identical to main terminal WS endpoint (#2)
- Close codes: identical to main terminal WS endpoint (#2)

#### GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/agents/{name}/terminal/info
- Auth: Required (standard bearer token)
- Path params: `{ws}` — workspace ID, `{name}` — agent name
- Response 200:
  ```json
  {
    "session_name": "ws-prefix-agent-name",
    "running": true
  }
  ```
- Response 404: workspace not found or agent session not found

## Dependencies
- Existing docs/api.md structure and conventions
- handlers_terminal.go, handlers_terminal_ws.go, handlers_terminal_spawn.go, handlers_terminal_sessions.go for exact request/response shapes
- terminal_auth.go for token generation/validation details
- terminal.go for TerminalManager constants (defaultMaxTerminalSessions=20, resizeMsgLen=5, etc.)
- workspace_context.go for WorkspaceMiddleware behavior (workspace validation, context injection)
- routes.go: lines 108-133 (current flat routes — 15 registrations, 10 covered by this spec), 236-244 (tab metadata already scoped), 261-267 (agent terminals already scoped)
- n28bt.7 (completed): tmux sessions namespaced by workspace ID

## Edge Cases & Error Handling
- **Session name with dots** (from issue IDs): sanitized to dashes by spawn handler before validation
- **Session limit reached** (default 20): rejected pre-WebSocket-upgrade with 503 and message "maximum terminal sessions reached"
- **Token replay**: nonce tracked in memory map, rejected with 401 on second use
- **Token expired** (>60s): rejected with 401
- **Race between scheduled kill and re-attach**: CancelPendingKill() called in Attach(), so re-attach always wins
- **Server restart**: generates new HMAC secret, all old tokens become invalid (by design, not a bug)
- **tmux binary not found**: TerminalManager creation fails at startup, all terminal endpoints return 503
- **close-all with Redis down**: tmux sessions killed but metadata cleanup fails; returns 200 with warning string, not 500
- **Concurrent WebSocket connections to same session**: each gets its own PTY attach with unique connID
- **Non-matching binary WebSocket messages** (wrong length or missing 0x01 marker): treated as terminal input bytes, written to PTY — no error returned
- **Workspace not found**: 404 from WorkspaceMiddleware before handler executes (response body: `{"error": "workspace not found: {ws}"}`)
- **Empty workspace ID in path**: 400 from WorkspaceMiddleware (response body: `{"error": "workspace ID is required"}`)
- **Cross-workspace session isolation**: tmux sessions prefixed by workspace ID (per n28bt.7 completed work), so identically-named sessions in different workspaces never collide

## Acceptance Criteria
- All 10 session lifecycle endpoints are documented with workspace-scoped paths `/api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/...`
- All 3 agent terminal endpoints are documented with paths `/api/workspaces/{ws}/agents/{name}/terminal/...`
- The resize protocol is documented as the correct 5-byte format `[0x01, cols_hi, cols_lo, rows_hi, rows_lo]`, NOT the old 4-byte uint32 format
- `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/terminal/sessions` response does NOT include `issue_id` field
- No flat `/api/terminal/...` paths appear anywhere in the spec (all workspace-scoped)
- Each endpoint specifies: auth requirements, path params, query params, request body (if any), all response status codes with shapes, and error conditions
- Close code 4001 semantics documented with frontend behavior guidance (show CrashOverlay, no auto-reconnect)
- WorkspaceMiddleware 400/404 error responses documented for all endpoints

## Testing Strategy
- Verify each endpoint entry in docs/api.md matches the actual handler implementation in the handlers_terminal*.go files
- Cross-reference request/response shapes against handler code and existing test files
- Confirm the resize protocol section uses the 5-byte format — grep for `resizeMsgLen` and `resizeMsgMarker` in handlers_terminal.go to verify
- Verify GET sessions response does NOT include `issue_id` — read handleListTerminalSessions to confirm
- Validate scope boundaries: no overlap with tab management (loomcli-wit5o), state persistence (loomcli-uzq7i), session history (loomcli-rocpq), or issue tabs (loomcli-aeilf)
- Check that all paths in the spec use `/api/workspaces/{ws}/` prefix with no flat route remnants
- After implementation: verify all routes are registered on wsMux behind WorkspaceMiddleware, and frontend TODO(workspace-routing) comments in terminal.ts are resolved
- Manual: compare documented response shapes against actual API responses from a running server

title: Fix hardcoded max-retries threshold in computeAgentStatus
description: computeAgentStatus in daemon_cmd.go:512 hardcodes RestartCount > 3 to show 'failed' status, ignoring the configured max_retries value. If max_retries is set to e.g. 10, agents show as 'failed' after 3 restarts while still being restarted. Fix: pass configured max_retries through SupervisedAgentStatus or as a parameter to computeAgentStatus.
design:
## Summary

computeAgentStatus in daemon_cmd.go:509 hardcodes the threshold RestartCount > 3 to determine if an agent has failed, ignoring the configured max_retries value from the daemon's restart policy. When a user configures max_retries to a value other than 3 (e.g., 10), agents are incorrectly shown as 'failed' after 3 restarts even though the daemon is still actively restarting them. The fix threads the configured maxRetries value from the daemon config through writeStateFile into computeAgentStatus, replacing the hardcoded constant.

## Technical Approach

The simplest and least disruptive approach is to add a `maxRetries int` parameter to both `computeAgentStatus` and `writeStateFile`. This avoids modifying the `SupervisedAgentStatus` struct (which would change the public API surface of `Daemon.Agents()`) and keeps the fix localized to the two functions and their call sites.

An alternative considered was adding a `MaxRetries` field to `SupervisedAgentStatus` so it travels with the agent data. This was rejected because max_retries is a daemon-level config, not a per-agent property, and embedding it in every agent status struct is semantically incorrect.

Another alternative was exposing `getMaxRetries` as a public method on `Daemon` and calling it from `writeStateFile`. This was rejected because it would require `writeStateFile` to take a `*Daemon` parameter, coupling the state-writing logic to the daemon type unnecessarily.

## Files to Modify

### 1. internal/cli/daemon_cmd.go

**computeAgentStatus** (line 509): Add `maxRetries int` parameter. Replace the hardcoded `3` with this parameter:
```go
func computeAgentStatus(ap SupervisedAgentStatus, maxRetries int) string {
    if ap.PID > 0 && lockfile.IsProcessRunning(ap.PID) {
        return "running"
    }
    if ap.RestartCount > maxRetries {
        return "failed"
    }
    return "stopped"
}
```

**writeStateFile** (line 469): Add `maxRetries int` parameter. Pass it through to `computeAgentStatus`:
```go
func writeStateFile(path string, startedAt time.Time, agents []SupervisedAgentStatus, maxRetries int) error {
```
And update the call on line 481:
```go
Status: computeAgentStatus(ap, maxRetries),
```

**Call site 1** (line 223): Pass max retries from the daemon config. The `daemon` variable is available in scope, but the cleanest approach is to extract maxRetries once before the loop:
```go
maxRetries := 3
if config.Daemon.RestartPolicy.MaxRetries != nil {
    maxRetries = *config.Daemon.RestartPolicy.MaxRetries
}
```
Then pass to both calls:
```go
if err := writeStateFile(stateFilePath, startedAt, daemon.Agents(), maxRetries); err != nil {
```

**Call site 2** (line 249, inside goroutine): Same — `config` is captured in the goroutine's closure:
```go
if err := writeStateFile(stateFilePath, startedAt, daemon.Agents(), maxRetries); err != nil {
```

Note: Extract the `maxRetries` variable once before both call sites (after config is available, before the goroutine) so both use the same value. The `config` variable is already in scope at line ~203.

### 2. internal/cli/daemon_cmd_test.go

**TestComputeAgentStatus_Running** (line 463): Update call to `computeAgentStatus(ap, 3)`.

**TestComputeAgentStatus_Stopped** (line 477): Update call to `computeAgentStatus(ap, 3)`.

**TestComputeAgentStatus_StoppedWithDeadPID** (line 491): Update call to `computeAgentStatus(ap, 3)`.

**TestComputeAgentStatus_Failed** (line 505): Update call to `computeAgentStatus(ap, 3)`.

**TestComputeAgentStatus_FailedBoundary** (line 519): Update call to `computeAgentStatus(ap, 3)`. The boundary tests already test against the default value of 3, so passing 3 maintains the same behavior.

**TestComputeAgentStatus_RunningOverridesRestartCount** (line 546): Update call to `computeAgentStatus(ap, 3)`.

**Add new test: TestComputeAgentStatus_CustomMaxRetries**: Verify that when maxRetries is set to a custom value (e.g., 10), an agent with RestartCount of 4 is "stopped" (not "failed"), and an agent with RestartCount of 11 is "failed":
```go
func TestComputeAgentStatus_CustomMaxRetries(t *testing.T) {
    tests := []struct {
        name         string
        restartCount int
        maxRetries   int
        want         string
    }{
        {"below custom limit", 4, 10, "stopped"},
        {"at custom limit", 10, 10, "stopped"},
        {"above custom limit", 11, 10, "failed"},
        {"zero max retries, no restarts", 0, 0, "stopped"},
        {"zero max retries, one restart", 1, 0, "failed"},
    }
    for _, tt := range tests {
        t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            ap := SupervisedAgentStatus{
                PID:          0,
                RestartCount: tt.restartCount,
            }
            status := computeAgentStatus(ap, tt.maxRetries)
            if status != tt.want {
                t.Errorf("computeAgentStatus(restartCount=%d, maxRetries=%d) = %q, want %q",
                    tt.restartCount, tt.maxRetries, status, tt.want)
            }
        })
    }
}
```

**TestWriteStateFile_Success** (line 564): Update call to `writeStateFile(stateFilePath, startedAt, agents, 3)`.

**TestWriteStateFile_AtomicWrite** (line 611): Update call to `writeStateFile(stateFilePath, startedAt, agents, 3)`.

## Files to Create

None.

## Dependencies

- No external packages needed.
- No other tasks need to be completed first.

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **MaxRetries is nil (default)**: Both call sites already handle this — extract to a local variable with default 3, matching existing behavior in `getMaxRetries()`.
2. **MaxRetries is 0**: This means "no retries allowed". An agent with RestartCount > 0 correctly shows "failed". The test covers this case.
3. **Consistency with daemon's shouldRestart**: The `Daemon.shouldRestart` method uses `d.getMaxRetries()` which reads the same config field. After this fix, `computeAgentStatus` will use the same configured value, ensuring the status display matches the actual restart behavior.
4. **Config changes at runtime**: The config is loaded once at startup and doesn't change. The `maxRetries` variable is extracted once, which is correct.

## Testing Strategy

1. **Unit tests**: All existing `computeAgentStatus` tests updated to pass `maxRetries` parameter. New `TestComputeAgentStatus_CustomMaxRetries` table test verifies custom values.
2. **Existing tests pass**: All existing `writeStateFile` tests updated to pass the default `maxRetries=3`, preserving existing behavior.
3. **Manual verification**: Run `go test ./internal/cli/ -run "TestComputeAgentStatus|TestWriteStateFile" -v` to verify all tests pass.
4. **Key scenarios**: Agent with restart count 4 and max_retries=10 shows "stopped" (not "failed"). Agent with restart count 11 and max_retries=10 shows "failed". Default behavior (max_retries=3) unchanged.

title: Pool reports 'daemon not running' when bd daemon is alive but overloaded
description:
## Summary

When the bd daemon's 100-slot semaphore is full, new connections are accepted then immediately closed. The pool's TryConnectWithTimeout returns nil,nil which maps to ErrDaemonNotRunning. This triggers circuit breaker open, causing a 17-second cascade of 503s — even though the daemon is alive and will recover in seconds.

## Root Cause

server_lifecycle_conn.go:101-104 — when semaphore is full:
  select {
  case s.connSemaphore <- struct{}{}:
      go s.handleConnection(conn)
  default:
      _ = conn.Close()  // immediately closed, no error sent
  }

client.go:133-148 — TryConnectWithTimeout health check fails because connection was torn down → returns nil, nil

pool.go:346 — nil client → ErrDaemonNotRunning

## Fix

1. bd daemon: Before closing overloaded connections, send a "server busy" response so the client can distinguish overload from dead daemon
2. Pool: Track last-known-alive timestamp. If socket file exists AND was recently reachable (within last 30s), return ErrPoolExhausted instead of ErrDaemonNotRunning. This prevents the circuit breaker from tripping on transient overload.
3. Consider reducing maxConns from 100 to 20 (100 concurrent SQLite connections on a 1-CPU server just creates more contention)

## Files
- third_party/beads/internal/rpc/server_lifecycle_conn.go:101-104 — semaphore-full rejection
- internal/rpc/client.go:133-148 — TryConnectWithTimeout nil,nil path
- internal/webui/daemon/pool.go:346 — ErrDaemonNotRunning mapping
- third_party/beads/internal/rpc/server_core.go:116 — maxConns=100

title: Kanban: Blocker tooltip should render above cards and show issue titles
description:
Two issues with the blocker badge tooltip on Blocked column cards:

1. Z-index: The tooltip renders behind/under the card below it, making it partially obscured. It should have a high z-index so it always renders above other cards.

2. Content: Currently only shows issue IDs (e.g. 'loomcli-00s'). Should also include the issue title truncated to a reasonable length (e.g. ~40-50 chars). Example: 'loomcli-00s: Create run_local.sh with mounted auth...' instead of just 'loomcli-00s'.
design:
## Summary

The blocker badge tooltip on Kanban board cards has two bugs: (1) the tooltip renders behind/below sibling cards due to CSS stacking context issues, and (2) it only displays issue IDs without titles. This fix addresses both by elevating the hovered card's z-index and threading `blocked_by_details` (which already includes titles) from the backend through to the tooltip display.

## Technical Approach

**Z-index fix:** Add `z-index: 10` to `.draggable:hover` in DraggableIssueCard.module.css. Each card wrapper (`.draggable`) has `position: relative`, so when hovered, z-index: 10 elevates the entire card (including its absolutely-positioned tooltip) above sibling cards. This is the standard pattern for tooltip overlap in card lists and doesn't interfere with drag-and-drop (DnD-kit manages its own overlay layer).

**Titles in tooltip:** The backend already populates `BlockedByDetails []BlockerRef` (with id, title, priority) on BlockedIssue — it just isn't threaded through the KanbanIssue response. The fix adds this field to KanbanIssue, passes it through the frontend data flow, and updates BlockedBadge to display `id: title` (truncated to ~45 chars).

**Trade-offs:** Considered rendering the tooltip above the badge (bottom: 100%) instead of below, but this would clip against the column header for top cards. The z-index approach is more robust. For titles, considered a separate API call, but the data is already available in the existing response — just not exposed.

## Files to Modify

### Backend (Go)

1. **`internal/webui/handlers.go`** (lines 36-43, 424-428)
   - Add `BlockedByDetails []types.BlockerRef` field to `KanbanIssue` struct with json tag `blocked_by_details,omitempty`
   - In the handler loop where blocked info is merged (~line 424-428), add: `ki.BlockedByDetails = bi.BlockedByDetails`

### Frontend - Types

2. **`internal/webui/frontend/src/types/issue.ts`** (lines 126-130)
   - Add `blocked_by_details?: BlockerRef[]` to the kanban-enriched fields section of the `Issue` interface (alongside existing `blocked_by`)

### Frontend - Data Flow

3. **`internal/webui/frontend/src/App.tsx`** (lines 114-138)
   - Update `BlockedInfo` type import/usage to include `blockedByDetails`
   - In both branches of `blockedIssuesMap` construction (kanban mode lines 120-123, fallback mode lines 132-134), include `blockedByDetails: issue.blocked_by_details ?? []`

4. **`internal/webui/frontend/src/components/KanbanBoard/KanbanBoard.tsx`** (lines 37-40, 297-299)
   - Add `blockedByDetails?: BlockerRef[]` to `BlockedInfo` interface
   - Pass `blockedByDetails` through to IssueCard at lines 297-299 and 321-323 (both card and overlay rendering)

5. **`internal/webui/frontend/src/components/DraggableIssueCard/DraggableIssueCard.tsx`** (lines 59, 79)
   - Thread `blockedByDetails` through cardProps (same pattern as existing `blockedBy` threading)

### Frontend - IssueCard

6. **`internal/webui/frontend/src/components/IssueCard/IssueCard.tsx`** (lines 35-54, 194-199)
   - Add `blockedByDetails?: BlockerRef[]` to `IssueCardProps` interface
   - Import `BlockerRef` type from `@/types`
   - Pass `issueDetails` to `BlockedBadge` component (new prop alongside existing `issueIds`)

### Frontend - BlockedBadge Component

7. **`internal/webui/frontend/src/components/BlockedBadge/BlockedBadge.tsx`** (lines 16-27, 33-41, 109-120)
   - Import `BlockerRef` from `@/types`
   - Add `issueDetails?: BlockerRef[]` to `BlockedBadgeProps` interface
   - Update `formatIssueList` to accept optional details array and return display strings like `id: truncated_title` when details are available. If a detail has an empty title, show just the id. Truncate titles to ~45 chars with ellipsis.
   - In render, prefer `issueDetails` over `issueIds` when available for building the display list

### Frontend - CSS

8. **`internal/webui/frontend/src/components/DraggableIssueCard/DraggableIssueCard.module.css`** (after line 12)
   - Add: `.draggable:hover { z-index: 10; }` — elevates hovered card above siblings so tooltip is visible

9. **`internal/webui/frontend/src/components/BlockedBadge/BlockedBadge.module.css`** (lines 59-64)
   - Increase `max-width` from `240px` to `320px` to accommodate title text
   - Add text truncation styles to `.tooltipItem`: `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap;`

## Files to Create

None.

## Dependencies

- No external packages needed
- Relies on existing `BlockerRef` type in both Go (`internal/types/types.go:936-940`) and TypeScript (`types/issue.ts:188-192`)
- Backend `client.Blocked()` already returns `BlockedByDetails` populated with titles and priorities — verified in both SQLite and memory storage implementations

## Edge Cases & Error Handling

1. **Orphaned blockers** (blocker ID exists but issue was deleted): Backend already handles this — returns `BlockerRef` with empty title and default priority 2. Frontend should display just the ID when title is empty.
2. **Missing details** (old cached responses without `blocked_by_details`): The field is optional (`omitempty` in Go, `?` in TS). When absent, fall back to displaying IDs only (current behavior). This ensures backward compatibility.
3. **Long titles**: Truncate to ~45 chars in `formatIssueList` with ellipsis. CSS also enforces truncation via `text-overflow: ellipsis` as a safety net.
4. **Z-index and drag-and-drop**: DnD-kit uses a DragOverlay with its own portal/z-index management (overlay class in DraggableIssueCard). Adding `z-index: 10` on hover won't interfere because: (a) it only applies on hover, not during drag, (b) the dragged card gets `opacity: 0.5` and the overlay renders separately.
5. **No blocked_by_details but issueIds present**: Component should fall back to rendering IDs only (backward compat with non-kanban usage like graph view).

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests to Update

1. **`BlockedBadge/__tests__/BlockedBadge.test.tsx`**:
   - Add tests for new `issueDetails` prop: when provided, tooltip shows `id: title` format
   - Test title truncation: long titles get truncated with ellipsis
   - Test empty title in details: falls back to showing just the ID
   - Test fallback: when `issueDetails` not provided but `issueIds` is, shows IDs only
   - Test `issueDetails` with >5 items: first 5 shown with "and N more..."

2. **`IssueCard/__tests__/IssueCard.test.tsx`**:
   - Add test that `blockedByDetails` prop is passed through to BlockedBadge

3. **`KanbanBoard/__tests__/KanbanBoard.test.tsx`**:
   - Update `BlockedInfo` type in tests to include `blockedByDetails`
   - Add test that details are passed through to IssueCard

### Manual Verification

1. Start the app, open Kanban board
2. Find a blocked card, hover over the blocker badge
3. Verify: tooltip appears ABOVE sibling cards (not obscured)
4. Verify: tooltip shows `loomcli-xxx: Issue title here...` format
5. Verify: long titles are truncated with ellipsis
6. Verify: drag-and-drop still works correctly on blocked cards
